clue.text: Compelled to use pressure in extremity

indicators.note: the clue says the pressure is in the extremity, so one word sits within the other

parts.note: an extremity is an end
to use pressure on something is to force it

explanation.surface: Someone driven to extreme measures, made to squeeze hard when things got desperate.
explanation.definitionFit: Being made to do something against your will is being compelled by authority, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Is included amongst those who are against rackets

indicators.note: the word is is placed among the letters for the opponents, signalling a container

parts.note: in a vote, the noes are those opposed
taken as written

explanation.surface: A complaint that someone is lumped in with protesters against shady business schemes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rackets' looks like criminal schemes, but here it means din.
explanation.definitionFit: A racket is a loud din, and noises in the plural match rackets in that sense.

clue.text: Alternative supported by the German command

indicators.note: in a down entry, a piece supported by another sits above it

parts.note: or introduces an alternative
der is a German word for the

explanation.surface: An alternative plan backed by a German officer's command.
explanation.definitionFit: An order is an instruction to be obeyed, a direct synonym of command.

clue.text: Arrive with fresh request to give admission

definitions.note: the phrase as an imperative asks someone to confess

parts.note: to arrive is to come
fresh linen is clean

explanation.surface: A newcomer turns up with a new plea to be let in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Admission' suggests entry, but here it means a confession.
explanation.definitionFit: The imperative idiom urges someone to own up, so it is a plea for a confession.

clue.text: Determined detectives in action

indicators.note: the detectives are placed in the action, a container

parts.note: a deed is an action
CID is the Criminal Investigation Department, the UK police detective branch

explanation.surface: Resolute police detectives springing into action.
explanation.definitionFit: Determined and decided both describe a firm, resolved state of mind; they are synonyms.

clue.text: Dramatist's method of payment without conflict

definitions.note: read as dramatist is, the 's being the link

indicators.note: in its old sense, without means outside, so the payment method surrounds the conflict

parts.note: COD is cash on delivery
war is conflict

explanation.surface: A playwright's way of getting paid without any fuss.
explanation.walkthrough: Noel Coward was an English playwright; 'without' here means outside, not lacking.
explanation.definitionFit: Noel Coward was a famous English playwright, so the surname names a dramatist.

clue.text: Located, we hear, and named

indicators.note: signals that the word for located is to be heard spoken, not read

parts.note: something located is sited

explanation.surface: Someone found, reported and identified by name.
explanation.definitionFit: To cite someone is to mention them by name, as in a report or citation.

clue.text: I hunt down suspect in murder mystery

indicators.note: suspect as an adjective means dubious, telling us the letters are not to be trusted in order

explanation.surface: A detective vows to track down the suspect in a murder case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Suspect' reads as the noun from the murder case, but works as the anagram signal on I HUNT DOWN.
explanation.definitionFit: The genre name is the everyday term for a detective story built around a killing.

clue.text: Resort is to arrange revels

indicators.note: arranging the words resort is puts their letters into a new order

explanation.surface: A holiday resort sets about organising its festivities.
explanation.definitionFit: To revel is to make merry noisily, which is what one does when carousing boisterously.

clue.text: Prudence West is on Benedictine

parts.note: W is the compass abbreviation for west
taken as written
Dom is the title of a Benedictine monk

explanation.surface: A woman called Prudence West has been drinking the Benedictine liqueur.
explanation.walkthrough: Prudence and West look like a person's name, and Benedictine like the liqueur.
explanation.definitionFit: Prudence is sound judgment, the same good sense meant by the synonym.

clue.text: Oil catch freely, being liberal

indicators.note: letting the letters of oil catch move freely rearranges them

explanation.surface: A generous helping of oil is caught without restraint.
explanation.definitionFit: Lower-case, the word means broad-minded or wide-ranging in tastes, matching liberal.

clue.text: Went back over and copied again

definitions.meaning: ... one's steps, went over a route again
traced a second time, as with a drawing

explanation.definitionFit: Retrace means both to go back along a path and to trace a drawing anew.

clue.text: You can't be sure when nursing them

definitions.text: You can't be sure when nursing them

parts.words: You can't be sure when nursing them
parts.note: one nurses misgivings, and having them means being uncertain

explanation.surface: A worried new nurse unsure about the patients in their care.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nursing' suggests caring for patients; here it is the idiom of harbouring misgivings.
explanation.definitionFit: Uncertainties are what leave you unsure, and the idiom is to nurse them.

clue.text: Supporters of family life waving weird banners

indicators.note: banners that wave are shaken about, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Pro-family campaigners marching with strange placards.
explanation.definitionFit: Earners who bring home the money support the household, keeping family life going.

clue.text: City area veto's damaged proportional representation?

parts.note: a city block is an area bounded by streets

indicators.note: the word veto is damaged, knocked out of shape

parts.note: veto's reads as veto is, so the letters are those of veto, the 's being a link

explanation.surface: A city district's veto is undermined by a fairer voting system.
explanation.walkthrough: A block vote is cast by a delegate in proportion to the members represented, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Each delegate's ballot counts in proportion to members represented, a whimsical take on the electoral term.

clue.text: Chill wine to go with last bits of turkey and cold game

parts.note: ice chills things
hock is German white wine

indicators.note: the final letters of the word turkey are taken

explanation.surface: A Christmas scene: chilled wine with leftover turkey and cold game meat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Last bits' takes the final two letters, EY. 'Cold game' looks like chilled venison, but it is a sport on ice.
explanation.definitionFit: The sport is played on a frozen rink, making it a winter game played in the cold.

clue.text: Payment made for an old servant?

definitions.meaning: a fee paid in advance to keep someone's services

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a fee securing services and a faithful household servant.

clue.text: Conclusion is to include North Carolina for criticism

indicators.note: the word for the conclusion takes in the state abbreviation

parts.note: a denouement is the conclusion of a story
NC is the postal abbreviation for North Carolina

explanation.surface: A story's ending expanded to feature North Carolina draws criticism.
explanation.definitionFit: A public condemnation is a harsh form of criticism, a near synonym.

clue.text: Wrong premise for making rules

indicators.note: a wrong premise is faulty, so its letters are put right in a new order

explanation.surface: A flawed assumption used as the basis for drawing up regulations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rules' looks like regulations; it means dominions, as a ruler's rules.
explanation.definitionFit: A ruler's realms or reigns are rules in the sense of territories governed.

clue.text: Mr A to Z in composing?

definitions.text: Mr A to Z in composing?

indicators.note: composing means putting together, here the letters of Mr A to Z in a fresh order

explanation.surface: A gentleman who covers everything from A to Z in composing music.
explanation.definitionFit: The Austrian composer was a master of every genre, so he was the complete A to Z of composition.

clue.text: Support in reverse

definitions.meaning: assistance or reinforcement held in reserve

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both reinforcement and driving backwards.

clue.text: Turn up with mother's cats

indicators.note: turning the word up puts its letters the other way round

parts.note: ma is mother, plus the possessive s

explanation.surface: Mother's cats appear when someone turns up.
explanation.definitionFit: These American big cats are also called cougars or mountain lions.

clue.text: Confined space where those inside call out

definitions.text: Confined space where those inside call out

parts.words: Confined space where those inside call out
parts.note: a cramped booth whose occupants make telephone calls out

explanation.surface: A cell where prisoners shout out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Call out' suggests shouting; here it is making a telephone call.
explanation.definitionFit: The red street booth is a cramped space for making telephone calls.

clue.text: Lack of excitement, yet Eastern nun is disturbed, I must conclude

indicators.note: I comes at the very end of the build
the nun is disturbed, so her letters are stirred up

explanation.surface: Things are dull, yet an Eastern nun is upset, I must conclude.
explanation.definitionFit: Ennui is listless boredom, the state of having nothing exciting to do.

clue.text: Sneak attending class with hesitation

parts.note: attending a place is being in it
a school class is a form
er is the sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: A sneaky pupil hesitates while attending class.
explanation.walkthrough: In British schools a FORM is a class or year group.
explanation.definitionFit: A sneak is a telltale who reports on others, just like a grass or snitch.

clue.text: US state taking a right from another

indicators.note: taking a right from the other state removes those letters from it

parts.note: a second US state, Arkansas
A plus R, the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: One US state annexing a strip of land from its neighbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Another' is a second US state, Arkansas; 'taking' removes A and R from its front.
explanation.definitionFit: Kansas is a Midwestern state of the USA.

clue.text: They're for putting on for party people

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both golf putting surfaces and members of an environmentalist party.

clue.text: Pen catalogues for elegant writers

parts.note: a pig pen is a sty
catalogues are lists

explanation.surface: A pen maker's catalogues aimed at those with fine handwriting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pen' suggests writing, but here it is an enclosure for pigs.
explanation.definitionFit: Writers admired for their polished prose style are called stylists.
